_README: Comments that license part of a ruling but are not in its `source` column.
A TSV row holds one URL because the front end binds `[href]="ruling.source"` directly,
but a ruling's text is often derived from more than one official comment: a curation
merge folds two restatements into one row, or an answer's caveat is resolved by a later
comment on the same rule. Verifying such a row against its single cited comment reports
`overstated` on text that is fully supported -- 12 of the first 15 overstated verdicts
were this, and the rest were real.
verify.py reads this file and adds the listed comments to the context and to the set of
official text the licensing-quote gate greps. So an entry widens what counts as
*supported*; it does not weaken the gate, which still requires a verbatim span.
Keys are `<ruling_id>@<card>`, matching verification.json. Add an entry only when the
extra comment genuinely licenses a clause -- an entry that does not is how a real
`overstated` gets silenced.
curate.py's merges are recovered automatically from curation.json's `superseded` lists
(see verify.py's merged_sources); this file is for everything else, added by hand.
propose.py reads this file too, in applied_comment_ids(). A comment folded into a row that
already exists never reaches the TSV's source column, so without this file every such
comment is re-proposed on every future refresh, forever. Recording it here is what makes a
fold stick -- the same job rejections.json does for a removal.
20 rows are listed. The backlog is larger and is worked through as rows are reviewed, so an
absent row means unreviewed, not clean.

why: Comment 42903 is the only official answer that addresses this scenario -- David
described the Red-Winged Parrot / Spangled Drongo interaction and Jamey said 'yes, it
counts' -- but he attached a condition: 'if the ability on the Spangled Drongo looks
for other players to gain nectar while taking the "gain food" action, it would not
count.' Comment 109108 (Jamey, 2024-12-28) resolves that condition: the Drongo
triggers on a nectar gain by any means, not only via the 'gain food' action. The
ruling carries the resolution instead of dropping the caveat, so it is licensed by
both comments.

Comment 35706 licenses that Snow Bunting counts. Which word qualifies it is comment 52267
(Jamey, 2022-05-01), answering 'Does snow bunting count? It's said snowy in the bonus
card.' with 'Yes, it counts.' -- the keyword is in the question, so the answer licenses it
only together with the question it replies to.
Comment 30838 licenses the conclusion. The reasoning -- and the fact that it holds even
though House Wren itself is a two-habitat bird -- is comment 55187 (Jamey, 2022-10-01),
answering a player who had lost this argument with Board Game Arena: 'Because the card is
referring to a "second" bird, it's looking at the first bird (and thus needs to follow the
same habitat as the first bird).'
The row cites the rules page, which states the bare reroll rule. Every clause added to it
comes from a named official answer, and all five agree:
51600 Jamey 2022-04-04  'At any time when gaining food, you can refresh the birdfeeder if
all dice show the same face' + 'If there's only 1 die in the
birdfeeder, all dice show the same face' + take the slug, then
refresh before choosing the next food
55217 Joe   2022-10-03  'This includes birds that are looking for a specific food and say
"if available."' (posted as a correction to Jamey's answer above
it, which was edited)
59705 Joe   2023-03-17  'for any reason' -- Emu with a single die left
63980 Joe   2023-10-30  'for any reason (cacheing included)'
64167 Jamey 2023-11-07  gaining 1 [die], and conditional 'if available' powers, both count
as gaining food
Five threads asked this and five answers said the same thing, which is why it is one
general ruling rather than five card rows. Proposals 20220404, 20221003, 20230317, 20231030
(part) and 20231107 are all folded in here.
